0.long_answer: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are widely used to relieve pain, reduce inflammation, and lower fever by inhibiting the COX enzymes, which in turn reduces the production of prostaglandins. These drugs can affect kidney function by reducing renal blood flow and altering electrolyte balance, which may lead to the retention of potassium and consequently elevated serum potassium levels (hyperkalemia). Indomethacin, for example, has been associated with an increase in serum potassium. Thus, while NSAIDs are effective for managing pain and inflammation, they can potentially cause hyperkalemia, especially in patients with compromised kidney function or those on other medications that influence potassium levels.
